title: Divide an Array Into Subarrays With Minimum Cost I
summary: Given an integer array nums of length n, divide it into three contiguous subarrays with the minimum total cost, where the cost of an array is defined as its first element.
statement: Given an integer array nums of length n, divide it into three contiguous subarrays with the minimum total cost, where the cost of an array is defined as its first element.
constraints: Partition nums into exactly three nonempty contiguous subarrays.
The cost is the sum of the first value of each subarray.
hints: The first subarray must begin at index zero.
The second and third starts may be any two distinct later indices in increasing order.
Choose the two smallest values in nums[1:] and add nums[0].
Any pair of later indices defines a valid three-part partition, so minimizing their values independently is sufficient.
editorial: Any pair of later indices defines a valid three-part partition, so minimizing their values independently is sufficient.

tests.explanation: The first value is fixed at one; choosing starts two and three gives total six.
All three single-element parts are forced, costing twelve.
